newsitem.title: FRANCE: Giscard urges Socialists to avoid damage over EU.
newsitem.headline: Giscard urges Socialists to avoid damage over EU.

text.p: Former centrist president Valery Giscard d'Estaing urged the opposition Socialists to avoid damaging France's place in Europe as the left scored a stunning victory in Sunday's parliamentary election runoffs.
"We must ask those who will govern France to be very careful not to cause too serious damage, notably to the situation of France in Europe," Giscard said.

Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin has said he will not impose extra austerity to qualify for a single European currency and has set four conditions for joining the euro from 1999, including participation of Italy and Spain from the start.

Giscard said the centre-right would continue to defend their views in opposition "without practising a scorched earth policy, that means without wishing bad things for France because power escapes us."
Giscard also criticised conservative President Jacques Chirac's decision to call the National Assembly election almost 10 months early.
"I think that people took a big risk of a negative vote by deciding to ask French citizens when it was known they were unhappy with they way they were governed," he said.
